subject: Hash/array deref of the wrong ref type must die "Not a HASH/ARRAY reference", not an SBCL type error
description:
op/avhv.t is 40/40 failing on ONE cause: every test checks that using an ARRAY ref as a hash dies with qr/^Not a HASH reference /.

IMPLEMENTED s317 for HASH / ARRAY / CODE. Two runtime helpers in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp (~1019): %p-wrong-referent-p (kind, value) — true only for DEFINITELY-wrong referents — and %p-not-a-ref (kind), signalling perl's exact text (a plain `error`, so p-eval-block's handler appends " at … line N.", supplying the trailing space avhv.t's regex needs). Guarded sites: p-gethash + (setf p-gethash) + p-ensure-hashref + p-cast-% (hash), p-aref + (setf p-aref) + p-ensure-arrayref + p-cast-@ (array), p-exists/p-delete/p-exists-array/p-delete-array, p-funcall-ref (code). 12 of 14 probe shapes byte-match real perl (scratchpad s317/nh2.pl); the must-not-die battery (s317/ok.pl) is unchanged.

PERFORMANCE RULE (s308), after a first wrong pass: every guard sits AFTER the fast path. p-gethash tests hash-table-p — the same test GETHASH did internally — first; p-aref and p-funcall-ref reach the predicate only once the normal branch failed. Zero added cost on correct code. Do NOT re-introduce the earlier shape (predicate first, with its string= on the kind) — that put a string compare on every hash read.

TWO DO-NOT-RETRYs, both found by the gate/sweep after probes said "clean":
1. NO SCALAR guard in p-cast-$. PCL COLLAPSES a scalar-ref-to-coderef, so that site legitimately receives a raw function — Sub::Quote's generated `my $x = ${$_[1]->{'$name'}};` is exactly that, and guarding took Moo down (6 rows of Pl/t/moo-01.t).
2. A REMAINING P-BOX IS NOT A MISMATCH. PCL's `\%h` is a DOUBLE box — box(box(hash-table)) — so unbox peeling one layer legitimately leaves a box the caller unboxes again (p-ensure-hashref returns it; (setf p-gethash) unboxes it). Including p-box-p in the mismatch sets broke `$refref->{k} = $v` and made perl-tests/postfixderef.t stop 4 tests early. Both reasons are recorded in the code.
   Diagnosis method worth reusing: ./runpl aborts too early to show which guard fires; instead log from %p-not-a-ref to a FILE plus (sb-debug:print-backtrace :count 6) and run the SWEEP — the backtrace named (SETF P-GETHASH-DEREF) and the double-box argument immediately.

RESULT ON THE SUITE: postfixderef.t 95 pass → 99 pass (4 rows FIXED, full 121 still run).

RESIDUE (open, needs a different mechanism): `$$aryref` still reads as the array, and `$scalarref->{k}` still raises SBCL's type error rather than "Not a HASH reference". Both need a referent-kind tag on the box (ir-spec-level decision), not a type-sniff at the deref site.</parameter>
</invoke>
